crops.name: Cassava
crops.guidance: Use clean planting material, inspect for cassava mosaic and bacterial blight symptoms, remove severely affected plants, and consult an extension worker before treatment.

crops.name: Maize
crops.guidance: Monitor leaves and cobs for insect damage, leaf spots, and stalk problems. Use integrated pest management and safe storage to reduce mould and aflatoxin risk.

crops.name: Sorghum
crops.guidance: Use locally recommended varieties, maintain field sanitation, monitor for shoot fly and fungal disease symptoms, and seek extension advice before applying products.

crops.name: Cowpea
crops.guidance: Inspect leaves, stems, pods, and roots. Use resistant varieties, clean seed, crop rotation, and integrated pest management; follow locally approved product labels.

crops.name: Rice
crops.guidance: Use clean seed, balanced nutrition, appropriate spacing, and field monitoring for blast and bacterial leaf blight. Confirm a diagnosis before treatment.

crops.name: Yam
crops.guidance: Select healthy seed yam, avoid damaged setts, use clean tools, and remove visibly diseased planting material. Ask an extension worker about local disease pressure.

crops.name: Millet
crops.guidance: Use adapted varieties, maintain weed and field sanitation, monitor for downy mildew and smut symptoms, and use only approved control measures.

healthTopics.name: Malaria warning signs
healthTopics.guidance: Fever, chills, and headache can occur with malaria but are not specific. Severe fatigue, confusion, convulsions, breathing difficulty, dark or bloody urine, jaundice, or abnormal bleeding require emergency care.

healthTopics.name: Anaemia
healthTopics.guidance: Tiredness, weakness, dizziness, and shortness of breath can have many causes. A health worker should confirm anaemia with appropriate testing and identify the cause.

healthTopics.name: Tuberculosis
healthTopics.guidance: Persistent cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss, or coughing blood need assessment at a health facility. Do not rely on an app to confirm or exclude tuberculosis.

healthTopics.name: Cholera and acute diarrhoea
healthTopics.guidance: Repeated watery diarrhoea can rapidly cause dehydration. Use safe oral rehydration guidance and seek urgent care for severe dehydration, inability to drink, blood in stool, or a very young or weak patient.

healthTopics.name: Meningitis danger signs
healthTopics.guidance: Severe headache, fever, neck stiffness, confusion, seizures, or a rapidly worsening condition require emergency assessment.

healthTopics.name: Jaundice
healthTopics.guidance: Yellowing of the eyes or skin can have several causes, including liver disease and severe infection. Arrange prompt clinical assessment, especially with fever, confusion, bleeding, or severe weakness.

healthTopics.name: Diabetes risk
healthTopics.guidance: Increased thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, or blurred vision need clinical testing. The app cannot diagnose diabetes from symptoms or a photograph.

healthTopics.name: Skin concern
healthTopics.guidance: Keep affected skin clean and dry and avoid sharing medicines or creams. Seek care for spreading redness, pus, severe pain, fever, facial swelling, or involvement of the eyes.
